scope: Two complete text reads with pinned Git blob verification. MD5 implementation statically reviewed; original runtime unavailable, no altered port used as proof.
findings: md5py explicitly describes an educational implementation, warns against production use, and states Python License. Root MIT screening is insufficient for copying it.

Python3 parsing fails at a long integer literal; additional old-style inequality, long/map(None)/string.join and division semantics need a port. Python2 executable was not available; independent digest vectors not run.
MD5.init resets state words, input and length but not count; reusing init after update retains the old length counter. Static finding, no Python2 execution.

update does not mask the low bit counter to 32 bits. Its overflow comparison is unsuitable for Python unbounded integers; large-input length qualification missing. Static finding, no multi-GiB input processed.
Original Hasher and rfigc source use hashlib rather than this educational module; these findings are not attributed to the active hashing path.

pyinstrument README distinguishes main-thread signal sampling from setprofile overhead and documents interference with sleeps/system calls. These historical statements and old Django timings were read, not verified on current Python/hardware.

README overhead table lists 5.33 seconds versus 1.46 seconds as 365 percent overhead: that is about 365 percent total time, about 265 percent additional time. Documentation numbers cannot be reused as measured optimization results.
